provenance.note: District Environment Plan: Satara (2018-19, Environment Department, Government of Maharashtra and Maharashtra Pollution Control Board), which carries no water-balance table: 10 figures the plan states about water, each transcribed with the sentence it was read from and the PDF page it sits on, and 5 of its water action points. Nothing is computed from the plan; a balance is served only where the plan prints one. Review status verified (checked against the document on 2026-09-01).

conventions.figures: value and unit as the plan states them; quote is the sentence verbatim; pdfPage is the viewer's page, printedPage the number printed on it
conventions.waterBalance: null when the plan carries no NGT-template balance; the page says so rather than estimating one
conventions.review: proposed until a person reads every figure against the PDF; then verified with the date
conventions.document: sha256 and byte length of the PDF as retrieved, so a re-posted file is detected; the PDF itself is not mirrored

document.title: District Environment Plan: Satara
document.publisher: Environment Department, Government of Maharashtra and Maharashtra Pollution Control Board
document.editionNote: The label MPCB's listing gives the plan; the PDF itself carries no year on its cover. Its metadata dates the file 30 December 2019 and the filename carries 23 June 2021, the date it was posted.
document.template: CPCB model District Environment Plan under NGT O.A. 360 of 2018 (order dated 26 September 2019): a profile table and gap-and-action tables per theme. It is not the NGT water-balance template and carries no demand, supply or deficit table.
quirks: The cover page header reads 'District Environment Plan: Latur'; every inner page header and the body read Satara.
The Koyna is spelled 'Konya' in the river list.

figures.label: Rivers named, with their length in the district
figures.detail: Krishna 160 km, Koyna 30 km, Venna 47 km, Nira 43 km, Urmodi 18 km; 13 nallas or drains meet them.
figures.quote: There are 5 Rivers in Satara district of approx. Krishna River - 160 km, Konya river - 30 km, Venna river – 47 km, Nira River- 43 km & Urmodi River - 18 km. 13 nos. of Nallas/Drains meet rivers.

figures.label: Sewage generated by the urban local bodies
figures.quote: ULB generate about 49.75 MLD of sewage with 21.5 MLD of STP.

figures.label: Sewage treatment capacity in the urban local bodies
figures.quote: ULB generate about 49.75 MLD of sewage with 21.5 MLD of STP.

figures.label: Sewage conveyance network
figures.detail: The plan attributes most of the treatment deficit to the short conveyance network.
figures.quote: Most of the deficit is accounted due to lack of sewage conveyance system of only 41.83 KM which in most of the ULBs.

figures.label: Bore-wells with permission to extract groundwater (estimate)
figures.quote: There are 85,562 nos. of estimated numbers of bore-wells to whom permissions is given for extraction of groundwater.

figures.label: Groundwater available
figures.detail: Stated without a source or an assessment year; IN-GRES assesses the district's annual extractable resource separately, and the two are not reconciled here.
figures.quote: 94,421 Ham of Groundwater available in Satara.

figures.label: Industries generating effluent
figures.detail: Agro-based and metallurgical units are the prominent types.
figures.quote: 1538 nos. of Industries generate 275.97MLD Effluent. Agro base/Metallurgical are prominent type of industries.

figures.label: Industrial effluent generated
figures.detail: From 1,538 industries; 38 of them are recorded as meeting standards.

figures.label: Additional sewage treatment capacity the plan calls for
figures.detail: An action point in Table 3, stated as approximate.
figures.section: Table 3 Action Plan for Water Quality Management

actionPoints.text: Thorough mapping of surface water resources, with an extensive assessment of quality
Criticality indicators to be established for each water body or resource
Extend the water-quality monitoring network, and set up online monitoring for surface water bodies
Approximately 60 MLD of sewage treatment capacity needed; strengthen the sewage collection network to cover the whole population
In situ treatment for river stretches, and a policy for reuse and recycling of treated wastewater
